svg.text: A hand-made ligand classification, tested against the method that never had a drop
anyone mining PDB ligands for binding sites or drug discovery
whether a declared additive label survives the size confound
declared additives sit on the size line like everything else
share of this component's entries that were solved by cryo-EM (log scale)

area is the number of entries carrying the component
the functional form decided the answer
Fitted linearly, the declared additives sit a mean +0.5 points from prediction with mixed
signs, and the classification looks like it tests negative. That fit predicts a negative
cryo-EM share for every component left of 10% on this axis, which cannot happen, and the
positive residuals it manufactures against the floor are its entire null. Fitted in log-odds —
the shape a bounded share actually has — 15 of 16 additives fall below prediction, by a median
of 28x. Both fits are drawn because only one of them can be right and they disagree
were declared additives and sit on the line
at 0.9x to 2.4x. They are also genuine
physiological ions, and the test says they
behave like one. MES at 146x, PEG at 150x,
ethylene glycol at 153x and MPD at 262x are
RCSB PDB search API, fetched 2026-09-22; the 30 most common non-polymer components, each crossed with exptl.method and with a molecular-weight
histogram of the entries carrying it. The grouping is declared in the script, not derived, which is what makes it testable. Host size is summarised as
the share of an entry's carriers over 200 kDa because the histogram is binned at 50 kDa and its median is quantised to the bin. Two components have no
cryo-EM entry at all and are placed by a Haldane correction, drawn dashed. A high cryo-EM share is not evidence of biology — it tracks host size,
which is what the conditioning is for; only the depleted end carries a mechanism. Components are multi-valued per entry and cannot be summed.
